readmeExcerpt:
The open source AI research agent.

## Install macOS / Linux: ```bash curl -fsSL https://feynman.is/install | bash ``` Windows (PowerShell): ```powershell irm https://feynman.is/install.ps1 | iex ``` Or with npm and Node.js 22.22 or newer: `npm install -g @companion-ai/feynman`. Then sign in to a model provider: ```bash feynman setup ``` The [installation guide](https://feynman.is/docs/getting-started/installation) covers pinned versions, uninstalling, and the skills-only bundle for Codex and OpenCode. The [setup guide](https://feynman.is/docs/getting-started/setup) covers local models and editors such as Zed. ## Use ```bash feynman "what do we know about scaling laws" feynman lit "RLHF alternatives" feynman deepresearch "mechanistic interpretability" ``` | Workflow | What it does | | --- | --- | | `/deepresearch ` | Planned investigation with parallel researchers and citation checks | | `/lit ` | Literature review: consensus, disagreements, open questions | | `/review ` | Critique with severity levels and a revision plan | | `/audit ` | Paper claims compared with its public code | | `/replicate ` | Replication plan; runs only after you choose an environment | | `/recipe ` | Ranked ML training recipes with datasets and code | | `/compare ` | Source comparison matrix | | `/draft ` | Paper-style draft from research findings | | `/autoresearch ` | Bounded experiment loop against a benchmark | | `/summarize ` | Summary of a paper, repository, or PDF | Results are saved to `outputs/` (drafts to `papers/`). `/lit`, `/deepresearch`, and `/recipe` also write a provenance file listing the sources used and what was verified. ## Sources Feynman searches alphaXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, arXiv, PubMed, Europe PMC, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Crossref, the web, and Hugging Face, and reads local PDFs and documents. Free `OPENALEX_API_KEY` and `SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY` keys avoid the shared rate limits. PubMed and Europe PMC full-text snippets preserve inline scientific terms and paragraph boundaries. It runs on stock [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) with four research agents: researcher, verifier, reviewer, and writer. Add your own tools, such as a Zotero library, with `feynman mcp add`. ## Telemetry Feynman sends anonymous usage data to PostHog: commands, workflows, tools, models, token counts, and errors with their messages and stack traces (your home folder shown as `~`). It never sends prompts, model output, paper content, or tool arguments. Turn it off with `FEYNMAN_TELEMETRY=off`. [What is sent](https://feynman.is/docs/getting-started/configuration#telemetry) ## Contributing ```bash git clone https://github.com/Companion-Inc/feynman.git cd feynman npm install npm test ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). [Docs](https://feynman.is/docs) · [Release notes](RELEASES.md) · [MIT License](LICENSE)
readmeHtml:
The open source AI research agent.

Install

macOS / Linux:

curl -fsSL https://feynman.is/install | bash

Windows (PowerShell):

irm https://feynman.is/install.ps1 | iex

Or with npm and Node.js 22.22 or newer: npm install -g @companion-ai/feynman.

Then sign in to a model provider:

feynman setup

The installation guide covers pinned versions, uninstalling, and the skills-only bundle for Codex and OpenCode. The setup guide covers local models and editors such as Zed.

Use

feynman "what do we know about scaling laws"
feynman lit "RLHF alternatives"
feynman deepresearch "mechanistic interpretability"
Workflow What it does
/deepresearch <topic> Planned investigation with parallel researchers and citation checks
/lit <topic or lab> Literature review: consensus, disagreements, open questions
/review <paper or draft> Critique with severity levels and a revision plan
/audit <paper> Paper claims compared with its public code
/replicate <paper> Replication plan; runs only after you choose an environment
/recipe <task> Ranked ML training recipes with datasets and code
/compare <topic> Source comparison matrix
/draft <topic> Paper-style draft from research findings
/autoresearch <idea> Bounded experiment loop against a benchmark
/summarize <source> Summary of a paper, repository, or PDF

Results are saved to outputs/ (drafts to papers/). /lit, /deepresearch, and /recipe also write a provenance file listing the sources used and what was verified.

Sources

Feynman searches alphaXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, arXiv, PubMed, Europe PMC, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Crossref, the web, and Hugging Face, and reads local PDFs and documents. Free OPENALEX_API_KEY and SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY keys avoid the shared rate limits. PubMed and Europe PMC full-text snippets preserve inline scientific terms and paragraph boundaries. It runs on stock Pi with four research agents: researcher, verifier, reviewer, and writer. Add your own tools, such as a Zotero library, with feynman mcp add.

Telemetry

Feynman sends anonymous usage data to PostHog: commands, workflows, tools, models, token counts, and errors with their messages and stack traces (your home folder shown as ~). It never sends prompts, model output, paper content, or tool arguments. Turn it off with FEYNMAN_TELEMETRY=off. What is sent

Contributing

git clone https://github.com/Companion-Inc/feynman.git
cd feynman
npm install
npm test

See CONTRIBUTING.md.

releases.name: v0.5.71
releases.body:
## v0.5.71 - 2026-11-16

- **pi-web-access 0.48.0.** DuckDuckGo searches are paced and share a cooldown, so they no longer get blocked after a few searches in a row. A search provider that times out now hands off to the next one instead of failing the search, and fetched pages come back more complete when the main extractor misses text. `feynman search set` accepts the new SpecStream, Autom, and cloro providers.

releases.name: v0.5.70
releases.body:
## v0.5.70 - 2026-11-14

- **Security patch: fast-xml-parser 5.12.1 and fast-xml-builder 1.3.2.** Fixes a quadratic-time attribute scan in the XML validator ([GHSA-7cfw-w2rf-f3jc](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7cfw-w2rf-f3jc)) and an uncontrolled recursion crash in the XML builder ([GHSA-g62r-xqpr-7fwx](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g62r-xqpr-7fwx)). arXiv, PubMed, and Europe PMC results parse the same as before.

releases.name: v0.5.69
releases.body:
## v0.5.69 - 2026-11-13

- **pi-subagents 0.88.1.** A permission prompt or other dialog that opens while the fleet inspector is up is no longer hidden behind it. `status` and `stop` no longer report a cleanly finishing background subagent as having ended without proof, and a manual `/compact` no longer wakes an idle parent while background subagents run.
- **Preserve JATS inline text.** PubMed and Europe PMC full-text results keep words inside inline markup in their original order, including subscripts and superscripts, without joining adjacent paragraphs. Section snippet limits and metadata are unchanged.
- **Patched hono.** Alpha Hub's MCP SDK now resolves hono 4.13.18 and @hono/node-server 2.1.8, which fix advisories published on November 12 (GHSA-4m76-xfj5-7975, GHSA-46wx-v44x-9hh2, GHSA-4h7h-rv7c-7m2v, GHSA-qv5m-9pm6-hqp3, GHSA-jpvv-r467-5p4w).

releases.name: v0.5.68
releases.body:
## v0.5.68 - 2026-11-11

- **pi-subagents 0.88.0.** A child waiting for your answer no longer runs out its `timeoutMs` while it waits, and a reply cut off at the model's output limit now fails instead of passing as a success. The subagent widget and `status` show the latest progress a running child reported. Copies of the parent session written by forked subagents are now deleted after `artifactConfig.cleanupDays`, so they no longer fill the disk. Also fixes Windows machines that block PowerShell and gateways that require a prompt cache key.
- **Paper search accepts `sort: "citation"`.** `feynman_science_database_search` recommends Semantic Scholar's default citation-count sort, and some models then passed `sort: "citation"`, which failed validation. The tool now treats `citation`, `citations` and `citation_count` as that default.

releases.name: v0.5.67
releases.body:
## v0.5.67 - 2026-11-10

- **Pi 1.5.2.**
  - Resuming a session whose project folder was moved or deleted now offers Continue, Fork or Cancel instead of only continuing; Fork copies it into the current folder so later resumes no longer ask.
  - The Anthropic default model is now `claude-opus-5-5`.
  - Pi's `cacheWarming` default is now `"idle"`, which keeps prompt caches warm for up to 30 minutes between runs and may change provider spend. Set `cacheWarming` to `"streaming"` to restore the old behaviour.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Terminal-based, open-source AI agent that automates deep technical research and information synthesis.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: The Feynman CLI provides a robust, open-source command-line interface dedicated to conducting autonomous AI-driven research. By executing directly from the terminal, it accepts a research prompt and autonomously scours numerous web sources, documentation, and papers. It seamlessly compiles scattered technical data into unified, easily comprehensible research briefs and summaries. The tool is explicitly designed to offload the manual burden of reading through extensive literature, delivering synthesized findings straight to the developer's workspace. It utilizes specialized agents for researching, reviewing, drafting, and verifying information.
keyFeatures: Command-line interface: Delivers a comprehensive autonomous research experience executing entirely within the terminal.
Automated web scraping: Autonomously navigates and extracts critical data from highly relevant technical sources and databases.
Deep synthesis: Parses and rewrites complex, multi-source topics into clear, digestible, and cited educational summaries.
Open-source core: Allows researchers to fully inspect and modify the underlying agentic reasoning and execution logic.
Simple installation: Provides a highly streamlined, single-command installation script tailored for UNIX systems.
Specialized sub-agents: Deploys dedicated agents for evidence gathering, internal critique, structured drafting, and rigorous citation verification.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers, students, and technical researchers seeking an open-source, terminal-native assistant to automate deep topical research. It specifically targets power users who demand rapid insights without the friction of manual web browsing.
